lines.cap: **Narrator:** This is Kavya. She is twelve. Friday, ten p.m., Block 512.
**Mum:** Uncle Raj's **wedding** in **London**! Every bag under **20 kg**, please!
**Dad:** London in June. My phone says **50 degrees**. Trust me, I did the maths: **shorts**.
**Kavya:** Dad, that's **50 °F**. **Fahrenheit**.
**Dad:** Fifty is fifty, Kavya.
**Ah Boy:** Are we there yet?
**Mum:** We haven't left the **flat**.
**Narrator:** But this documentary is about the little word after every number.
**Monsieur Mètre:** Monsieur Mètre. I am the **metre**. Born in Paris, 1791. My job: every number gets a **unit**.
**Monsieur Mètre:** 'Twenty'? Twenty **what**? Grams? Elephants? A number without a unit is just **gossip**.
**Narrator:** 1999. NASA loses a spacecraft at Mars. One team used **imperial** units, the other **metric**.
**Monsieur Mètre:** **US$125 million**. Pouf. **Mix your units**, and a spacecraft falls on Mars.
**Monsieur Mètre:** This family flies **11 000 km** tomorrow. I am coming too.
**Narrator:** Lost in Conversion. Episode 8: Are We There Yet?
**Officer Siti:** Liquids: **100 ml** or less per bottle, please.
**Dad:** My shampoo is **0.25 l**. That's way less than 100. Trust me, I did the maths.
**Monsieur Mètre:** Units, please! Litres **and** millilitres? **Same unit first!**
**Monsieur Mètre:** My family: **kilo**, **× 1000**. **Centi**, one **hundredth**. **Milli**, one **thousandth**.
**Officer Siti:** Two hundred and fifty. Too big, sir. Goodbye, shampoo.
**Mum:** Mine is **8 cl**: 8 × 10 = **80 ml**. Allowed.
**Monsieur Mètre:** **Golden rule.** **Smaller** unit, **more** of them: **multiply**. **Bigger** unit: **divide**.
**Ah Boy:** Check-in! Look! My bag is **4250**!
**Dad:** Four thousand?! The limit is **20**!
**Kavya:** It's **grams**, Dad. Kilograms are bigger, so divide: 4250 ÷ 1000 = **4.25 kg**.
**Dad:** Four ways to Gate C. Not the **79 500** one: biggest number.
**Kavya:** All in **metres**: 800, 750, 810. And 79 500 mm ÷ 1000 is just **79.5 m**!
**Ah Boy:** So phones go in **mm**, and flights go in **km**!
**Monsieur Mètre:** A **sensible** unit for a sensible number. Ah Boy, you are my favourite.
**Narrator:** Gate C. Cabin bags must fit the measuring frame: **55 cm by 40 cm by 20 cm**.
**Lita:** Hi! I'm **Lita**! A **10 cm** cube: 10 × 10 × 10 = **1000 cm³**. Exactly **one litre**!
**Lita:** Each little **1 cm** cube in me is **1 ml**. **1 cm³ = 1 ml**.
**Ah Boy:** I'm only about **25 litres**. Of boy. I fit!
**Mum:** You are **not** hand luggage.
**Narrator:** Seat 47A. The blanket: **2 m by 1.5 m**.
**Dad:** **3 m²**. And 1 m = 100 cm, so **300 cm²**. Trust me, I did the maths.
**Lita:** No! One square metre is **100** little squares along, and **100** rows.
**Lita:** **1 m² = 100 × 100 = 10 000 cm²**. **Square it** for area!
**Kavya:** Or change the **lengths** first: 200 × 150 = **30 000 cm²**. Same!
**Lita:** Volume? **Cube it**: **1 m³ = 1 000 000 cm³ = 1000 litres**. A thousand of me!
**Dad:** Thirty thousand square centimetres of blanket. Still cold.
**Flip:** Flip! Departures! London, **23:35**! Clack clack!
**Dad:** It's **22:45**. The gate shuts at **23:10**. 2310 − 2245 = **65 minutes**. Curry puff time.
**Flip:** An hour has **60** minutes, not 100! **Count on!**
**Kavya:** **15 min** to 23:00, then **10 min** to 23:10. Only **25 minutes**!
**Mum:** RUN!
**Narrator:** The flight: **13 h 50 min**. In June, London is **7 hours behind**.
**Kavya:** 23:35 + 13 h = 12:35. + 50 min = **13:25** tomorrow, Singapore time.
**Flip:** Back **7 hours**: **06:25** in London!
**Ah Boy:** Are we there yet?
**Flip:** Time to London: **2.4 h**!
**Ah Boy:** Two hours **forty** minutes. Easy.
**Ah Boy:** Are we there yet?
**Flip:** Two hours. Twenty-three minutes.
**Kavya:** **900 km/h**, and **2160 km** to go. Where does **2.4 h** come from?
**Trish:** Trish! The **DST triangle**! **D**istance on top, **S**peed and **T**ime below.
**Trish:** Cover **S**: **speed = distance ÷ time**. Cover **D**: **distance = speed × time**.
**Dad:** Takeoff: **150 km** in **20 minutes**. 150 ÷ 20 = **7.5 km/h**. Slower than a bicycle.
**Trish:** **Units must match!** Hours, not minutes. 20 min = 20 ÷ 60 = **⅓ h**.
**Kavya:** 150 ÷ ⅓ = 150 × 3 = **450 km/h**. A very fast bicycle.
**Ah Boy:** And in metres **per second**?
**Ah Boy:** I run **5 m/s**! Back the other way, **× 3.6**: **18 km/h**!
**Mum:** Not in the aisle, you don't.
**Uncle Raj:** Uncle Raj! Welcome! I'm **six foot one**, **twelve stone**, and home is **ninety miles** away!
**Monsieur Mètre:** Feet? Stone? **Miles?!**
**Sir Miles:** **The mile.** A thousand Roman paces. **About 1.6 km**. Give or take.
**Sir Miles:** It's **approximate**, so we write **≈**: **5 miles ≈ 8 km**.
**Ah Boy:** Miles → km: **× 1.6**. Km → miles: **÷ 1.6**. The **km** number is always **bigger**!
**Dad:** Limit **70 mph**? Slower than our **90 km/h**.
**Kavya:** 70 × 1.6 ≈ **112 km/h**. Faster, Dad.
**Narrator:** The drive: **60 miles at 60 mph**, a **30-minute** tea stop, then **30 miles at 20 mph**.
**Dad:** Average: 60 and 20, so **40 mph**. Trust me, I did the maths.
**Trish:** No! **Average speed = total distance ÷ total time**. Stops count!
**Trish:** On the **distance–time graph**: **steep** is fast, **flat** is stopped.
**Ah Boy:** Are we there yet?
**Uncle Raj:** Actually... yes.
**Narrator:** A London supermarket. Mum is cooking **vegetable biryani** for the wedding.
**Mum:** Rice: **2 kg for £6.80**, or **5 kg for £17.50**. Bigger is always cheaper.
**Kavya:** **Per** kg means **divide**: 6.80 ÷ 2 = **£3.40 per kg**. 17.50 ÷ 5 = **£3.50 per kg**. The small bag wins!
**Dad:** Juice: **750 ml for £2.10**, or **2 l for £5.40**. 750 is way more!
**Mum:** This time the big one wins. **Lowest price per unit** wins.
**Ah Boy:** My pillow is **1 kg**. Mum's rice is **1 kg**. Why is my pillow so **big**?
**Trish:** New letters! **Density = mass ÷ volume**. **M** on top, **D** and **V** below.
**Trish:** Feathers: **low density**. Little mass in each **cm³**, so 1 kg needs lots of **volume**.
**Uncle Raj:** My ice: **460 g** at **0.92 g/cm³**. Volume = 460 ÷ 0.92 = **500 cm³**.
**Kavya:** As water, at **1 g/cm³**, just **460 cm³**. Less dense than water **floats**; more dense **sinks**.
**Uncle Raj:** Like my **gold** cufflink. **19.3 g/cm³**. Oh. It's in my tea.
**Mum:** Souvenirs, all in **pounds**. Say **£1 = $1.70**. I am **not** multiplying all day.
**Kavya:** Join them with a **ruler**. The **third point** is your check.
**Monsieur Mètre:** And **check the scale**! One small square across is **£5**.
**Ah Boy:** Snow globe, **£40**! Up to the line... across... **$68**!
**Mum:** Sixty-eight dollars. For snow. In **June**.
**Dad:** Suit rental: **£350**. That's off the graph!
**Dad:** On second thoughts, shorts are fine for a wedding.
**Kavya:** A straight line **through the origin**: pounds and dollars are in **direct proportion**.
**Monsieur Mètre:** And the **gradient** is the **rate**: **$1.70** up for every **£1** across.
**Dad:** **10 °C** is **50 °F**. This afternoon, **20 °C**: double! So **100 °F**!
**Kavya:** Straight, but it **misses the origin**: **0 °C = 32 °F**. So **not** direct proportion.
**Narrator:** The wedding. Uncle Raj's lawn is a **hectare**: **100 m by 100 m**, **10 000 m²**. Mum wears **stilettos**.
**Mum:** Why do my heels **sink**, and your big feet don't?
**Trish:** New letters! **Pressure = force ÷ area**. **F** on top, **P** and **A** below.
**Trish:** Force is in **newtons**, **N**. **1 kg** weighs about **10 N**.
**Kavya:** Mum: **600 N** on a heel tip of **1 cm²**. 600 ÷ 1 = **600 N/cm²**.
**Uncle Raj:** An **elephant**: **50 000 N** on **5000 cm²** of feet. 50 000 ÷ 5000 = just **10 N/cm²**.
**Ah Boy:** Your heel presses **60 times** harder than an elephant, Mum!
**Mum:** I'll take that as a compliment.
**Trish:** Same force, **smaller area**: **bigger pressure**. Sharp knives. Wide snowshoes.
**Kavya:** **N/m²** are **pascals**, Pa. **1 N/cm² = 10 000 N/m² = 10 000 Pa**.
**Dad:** That's why I wore **sandals**. Big area. Trust me, I did the maths.
**Narrator:** For once, he did.

chapters.title: The family saves you some marks

lines.cap: **Narrator:** Before the credits, the family would like to save you some marks.
**Dad:** One. **30 km in 20 min** is not 1.5 km/h. Hours first: it's **90 km/h**. Ask me how I know.
**Lita:** Three. **5 m² = 50 000 cm²**, not 500. Square it!
**Flip:** Four. **13:45** to **14:10** is **25 minutes**, not 65. Count on!
**Uncle Raj:** Five. Average speed: **total distance ÷ total time**. Not the mean of the speeds. Tea stops count.
**Mum:** Six. Best buys: **same units** first. Grams with grams, millilitres with millilitres.
**Narrator:** Lost in Conversion will return.
**Narrator:** Changi. Baggage reclaim. Every suitcase arrives. Almost.
**Dad:** Where's my suitcase? I wrote **20** on the tag.
**Monsieur Mètre:** Twenty... what?
**Narrator:** Meanwhile, on Mars.
**A Martian:** Shorts? It's **minus sixty degrees** here.
